text:
Sam (Customer): hey @Mike we started getting intermittent 401s from Redwood after upgrading to the v2 Go SDK today. Local dev is fine, but our prod CI is failing a handful of requests with `unexpected status 401` and the SDK retries immediately (still 401).

Sam (Customer): quick repro: update go.mod from `github.com/redwood/inference-go` -> `github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2` and add a replace to point to our fork for a hotfix. build works, but when running against hosted API tokens are rejected.

Sam (Customer): go.mod snippet:
```
module github.com/ourservice/backend

require (
  github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 v2.1.3 // indirect
)

replace github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 => ../redwood-fork
```

Sam (Customer): logs show the request without Authorization on retry: `GET /v1/chat 401 unauthorized` - curl to the same endpoint with the same token succeeds.

Mike (Support): thanks—can you paste `go list -m all` and the actual error stack/log lines? also confirm whether your fork's go.mod has `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2` (it must include /v2 for v2 modules).

Sam (Customer): pasted output (trimmed):
```
github.com/ourservice/backend
github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 v2.1.3
github.com/redwood/inference-go v0.0.0-20220101010101-abcdef123456 // via replace
```

Sam (Customer): and our fork's go.mod currently says `module github.com/redwood/inference-go` (no /v2). Oops.

Mike (Support): yep that is the culprit. If the replaced module's go.mod doesn't match the import path (`/v2`), Go can end up building two copies or mismatched symbol sets. That can surface as auth middleware not being applied or duplicated transports, which looks like missing Authorization on retries.

Mike (Support): quick workarounds to try:
- ensure your fork's go.mod has `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2` and tag a v2 release (semantic import path)
- or remove the replace and `go get github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2@v2.1.3` to use the upstream tag
- run `go clean -modcache` and `GOPROXY=direct go build` after fixing module path
- as a short-term workaround vendor the SDK into your repo so there's a single module copy

Jia (Eng): adding: also run `go list -m -json github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2` to confirm module path used at build time. We hit this class of issue before when forks didn't update the module path for v2.

Lisa (Eng-ML): a note: if your CI is fronted by a proxy/load-balancer that returns redirects, the default http.Client can drop Authorization on redirect for some code patterns. But given curl works and local works, it strongly points to the module duplication mismatch Mike mentioned.

Sam (Customer): thanks. changed fork go.mod to `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2`, bumped tag to v2.1.4-pre and removed the local replace. did `go clean -modcache` and `GOPROXY=direct go get ./...` then rebuilt in CI.

Sam (Customer): CI run: previously ~5% of calls 401. After fix: 0/500 calls 401 across the same test suite. Looks fixed. :tada:

Mike (Support): great news — sounds like the fix stuck. We'll log this as a support KB: "Replace forks must use semantic import path for major v2+ (include /v2) or duplicate modules can break middleware/auth."

Jia (Eng): follow-up for eng: we should add a clearer diagnostic when the SDK detects duplicated module instances (error that suggests `go list -m all` mismatch). I can open a small PR to add a runtime warning.

deploy-bot: redeploy inference-go v2.1.4-pre -> staging (ci-20280301)

Sam (Customer): thanks everyone for the fast help — appreciate the clear repro steps.

Mike (Support): np — closing, but ping us if anything else crops up.
